title: The category of formal glueing data Glue(R -> S, f_1, ..., f_t)
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $f_1,\dots,f_t\in R$. Notation: for an $R$-module $P$ and $f\in R$, $P_f$ is the localization of $P$ at $f$ and $h_f:P_f\to Q_f$, $p/f^e\mapsto h(p)/f^e$, the localization of an $R$-linear map $h:P\to Q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] (for the multiplicative set $\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$, so $P_f$ is the module of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]); $R_f$ is the localized ring [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. For an $S$-module $P$, $P_f$ is its localization as an $R$-module, made an $S$-module by the localizations $(s\cdot)_f$ of the multiplications by the elements $s\in S$ (that these form an $S$-module structure, and that $h_f$ is $S$-linear when $h$ is, is clause (1) of the statement recorded in `pointers`). $P\otimes_RS$ and $h\otimes_RS$ are the base changes [def-weil-module-base-change]. For an $R$-module $P$ and $f,g\in R$ two canonical $R$-linear maps are used: $\sigma^P_{f,g}:(P_f)_g\to(P_g)_f$, $(p/f^a)/g^b\mapsto(p/g^b)/f^a$, and $c^P_f:(P\otimes_RS)_f\to P_f\otimes_RS$, $(p\otimes s)/f^e\mapsto(p/f^e)\otimes s$ (an $S$-linear map); $\sigma^P_{f,g}$ is the $R$-linear map with $(p/1)/1\mapsto(p/1)/1$ and $c^P_f$ the $R$-linear map with $(p\otimes s)/1\mapsto(p/1)\otimes s$ (that each exists, is unique with this property and is given by the displayed formula, and that $c^P_f$ is $S$-linear, are clauses (2) and (3) of the statement recorded in `pointers`; they are made from the universal property of the localization map $P\to P_f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]).

The category $\mathrm{Glue}(R\to S,f_1,\dots,f_t)$ of *glueing data* has as objects the systems $\mathbf M=(M',(M_i)_{i},(\alpha_i)_{i},(\alpha_{ij})_{i,j})$, $1\le i,j\le t$, where $M'$ is an $S$-module, $M_i$ is an $R_{f_i}$-module (regarded as an $R$-module through $R\to R_{f_i}$), $\alpha_i:M'_{f_i}\to M_i\otimes_RS$ is an $S$-linear isomorphism and $\alpha_{ij}:(M_i)_{f_j}\to(M_j)_{f_i}$ is an $R$-linear isomorphism, such that
(a) $(\alpha_{ij}\otimes_RS)\circ c^{M_i}_{f_j}\circ(\alpha_i)_{f_j}=c^{M_j}_{f_i}\circ(\alpha_j)_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{M'}_{f_i,f_j}$ as maps $(M'_{f_i})_{f_j}\to(M_j)_{f_i}\otimes_RS$, for all $i,j$; and
(b) (cocycle condition) $(\alpha_{jk})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{M_j}_{f_i,f_k}\circ(\alpha_{ij})_{f_k}=\sigma^{M_k}_{f_i,f_j}\circ(\alpha_{ik})_{f_j}\circ\sigma^{M_i}_{f_j,f_k}$ as maps $((M_i)_{f_j})_{f_k}\to((M_k)_{f_j})_{f_i}$, for all $i,j,k$.
A morphism $\mathbf M\to\mathbf N=(N',(N_i),(\beta_i),(\beta_{ij}))$ is a family $(u',(u_i)_i)$ of an $S$-linear map $u':M'\to N'$ and $R$-linear maps $u_i:M_i\to N_i$ such that $\beta_i\circ u'_{f_i}=(u_i\otimes_RS)\circ\alpha_i$ and $\beta_{ij}\circ(u_i)_{f_j}=(u_j)_{f_i}\circ\alpha_{ij}$ for all $i,j$. Composition and identities are componentwise: $(v',(v_i))\circ(u',(u_i))=(v'\circ u',(v_i\circ u_i))$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf M}=(\mathrm{id}_{M'},(\mathrm{id}_{M_i}))$; $\mathrm{Glue}(R\to S,f_1,\dots,f_t)$ is a category [def-nagata-category]. (An $R$-linear map between modules on which $f$ acts bijectively is $R_f$-linear, so the $u_i$, $\alpha_i$, $\alpha_{ij}$ are linear over $R_{f_i}$, $S_{f_i}$, $R_{f_if_j}$ respectively, as in the source.) (Stacks writes conditions (a) and (b) as $\alpha_{ij}\circ\alpha_i=\alpha_j$ and $\alpha_{jk}\circ\alpha_{ij}=\alpha_{ik}$, leaving the maps $c$ and $\sigma$ implicit.)

split_report.summary: Checked against More on Algebra Remark 05EL (more-algebra.tex 24640-24690, label remark-glueing-data, Section 05E5 section-formal-glueing; tags verified in tags/tags: 05E5, 05EL, 07K0 algebra-lemma-universal-property-localization-module, 00DK algebra-lemma-tensor-localization) and against the two citers, lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-isogeny (steps 2-4: objects D, D', morphisms Phi, Phi', componentwise composition and the components of an isomorphism) and prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence (Can(M), Can(u), c, sigma). (a) Completeness and correctness: objects (M', M_i, alpha_i, alpha_ij) with M' an S-module, M_i an R_{f_i}-module, alpha_i : M'_{f_i} → M_i ⊗_R S, alpha_ij : (M_i)_{f_j} → (M_j)_{f_i} isomorphisms, and conditions (a), (b) agree with 05EL (1)(a),(b) once the implicit identifications are written; I typed every composite: (a) is a pair of maps (M'_{f_i})_{f_j} → (M_j)_{f_i} ⊗_R S and (b) a pair ((M_i)_{f_j})_{f_k} → ((M_k)_{f_j})_{f_i}, both sides of each have these source and target. The source writes the target of (a) as (M_j)_{f_i}, which omits ⊗_R S (a slip of notation, not a mathematical error; the node has the right target). Morphisms (u', u_i) with the two compatibilities agree with 05EL (2). Composition and identities are componentwise (now written out); the remark that R-linear maps between modules on which f acts bijectively are R_f-linear (one line: f·u(x/f) = u(x)) reconciles 'S-linear'/'R-linear' with the source's isomorphisms of S_{f_i}-, R_{f_if_j}-modules; 'M_i regarded as an R-module' added. No mathematical error found. (b) Claims moved out: the existence, uniqueness, formula and S-linearity of sigma^P_{f,g} and c^P_f, that they are isomorphisms, and the S-module structure on P_f with the functoriality of h ↦ h_f, are the new unsplit statement node lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps, recorded in `pointers` (not in stmt_deps, to keep the definition from citing a lemma about its own data); the sentence of the statement that asserted them now refers to that statement in words. 'Can(M) is an object' and 'Can is a functor' are not in the definition (they are prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence (1)). (c) stmt_deps: kept def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-module-base-change; added def-weil-pbc-module-localization (it, not the -away node, defines the localization h_f of a linear map and the localized multiplications) and the Mathlib leaf def-nagata-category (CategoryTheory.Category).
